events.title: The feast of St. Joseph the Worker is instituted
events.shortBlurb: Pius XII set a Christian feast of labor on the first of May, honoring the carpenter of Nazareth…
body: The first of May had been, since the Second International adopted it in 1889 to honor the dead of the Haymarket riot in Chicago, the great festival of socialist and communist labor. In postwar Italy the day carried heavy political charge, and Catholic workers' associations longed for an observance of their own to set against the summons to class struggle.

On 1 May 1955, addressing Italian Catholic workingmen in Saint Peter's Square, Pius XII announced the new feast of Saint Joseph the Worker for that very day. A decree of the Congregation of Rites followed, setting the carpenter of Nazareth before laborers as their model, in whom human work is ennobled because the Son of God once shared it.

The memorial took the place of the Solemnity of Saint Joseph, patron of the universal Church, which Pius IX had instituted in 1870 and which had wandered through Eastertide on a moveable Wednesday. The change belonged to Pius XII's simplification of the calendar in 1955; the older feast of 19 March remained the principal day of Saint Joseph.

sources.text: Vatican, Address of Pope Pius XII on the Feast of St. Joseph the Worker (vatican.va)
